label: Refill garrison
summary: Refills the garrison (the troops defending a province) of the province.
details: Vanilla always writes `yes`. The game's documentation line ends with a stray `refill_levy = yes/no`, which looks copied from the levy effect, so the exact value rules are not documented.

label: Refill levy
summary: Refills the levy (the troops the province can raise) of the province.
details: Vanilla always writes `yes`. The game's documentation names `yes/no` as the values.

label: Refill supply
summary: Fills the army's supply up to its maximum capacity.
details: Works on an army. The game's documentation example misspells the key (`refull_supply`); the key is `refill_supply = yes`. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Reforge artifact
summary: Reforges the artifact: its durability is restored and other properties can be changed.
details: Fields left empty are not changed. Durability becomes the maximum unless you set it. The game's documentation notes that the current scopes are used implicitly, as in the artifact visuals definitions (common/artifacts/visuals). Vanilla uses it with a block, mostly to set an artifact's type, template, visuals, modifier, name and description; the description keys it uses ("melted") suggest it swaps a Santiago artifact to a melted-down form, which is an inference from the key names.

fields.name: rarity
fields.text: The new rarity, for example legendary.

fields.name: type
fields.text: The inventory slot type, for example trinket.

fields.name: modifier
fields.text: A static modifier that applies to the character who wields the artifact.

fields.name: max_durability
fields.text: A maximum durability that overrides the one the game's defines assign.

fields.name: decaying
fields.text: Whether the artifact loses durability over time.

fields.name: history
fields.text: A custom history entry, for example to record that someone other than the owner reforged it.
fields.values: a block with a type, such as reforged, created, stolen or inherited

fields.name: template
fields.text: A scripted base template with its own triggers and modifiers.

fields.name: generate_history
fields.text: Whether a new history entry is made automatically when none is scripted.

fields.name: quality
fields.text: The new quality, used in the AI's scoring.

fields.name: wealth
fields.text: The new wealth, used in the AI's scoring.

fields.name: creator
fields.text: A custom creator of the artifact.

fields.name: visuals_source
fields.text: Where the coat of arms graphics come from. Only a few artifact models use it, banners most notably.

label: Refund all perks
summary: Gives the character back every perk they have taken.
details: Written as `refund_all_perks = yes`. The game's documentation does not say what happens to the spent points beyond "refunds".

label: Refund lifestyle perks
summary: Gives back all the perks the character has taken in one lifestyle.
details: The value is the lifestyle, for example `intrigue_lifestyle`. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Release from prison
summary: Lets the character out of prison.
details: Vanilla always writes `release_from_prison = yes`. The game's documentation also mentions `imprison = X`, which does not match this key; vanilla only uses `yes`.

label: Remove acclaimed knight
summary: Takes the acclaimed knight off the accolade and hands the accolade to the successor, if there is one.
details: Written as `remove_acclaimed_knight = yes`, inside an accolade. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Agent slot
summary: Removes the given agent slot from the scheme.
details: The value is a saved scope holding the slot. Vanilla passes slots it saved earlier, such as `scope:slot_temp` or `scope:slot_1`.

label: All character modifier copies
summary: Removes every copy of the named modifier from the character.
details: The value is the modifier's name. Use it when the same modifier may be on the character more than once. Vanilla uses it with modifier names.

label: All county modifier copies
summary: Removes every copy of the named modifier from the county.

label: All dynasty modifier copies
summary: Removes every copy of the named modifier from the dynasty.

label: All house modifier copies
summary: Removes every copy of the named modifier from the house.

label: All house unity modifier copies
summary: Removes every copy of the named modifier from the house's unity.
details: Runs on a house. The value is the modifier's name.

label: All legend county modifier copies
summary: Removes every copy of the named modifier from the effect a legend has on its counties.
details: Runs on a legend.

label: All legend owner modifier copies
summary: Removes every copy of the named modifier from the effect a legend has on its owner.
details: Runs on a legend.

label: All legend province modifier copies
summary: Removes every copy of the named modifier from the effect a legend has on its provinces.
details: Runs on a legend.

label: All province modifier copies
summary: Removes every copy of the named modifier from the province.

label: Remove all realm laws
summary: Removes every realm law from the character.
details: This leaves all law groups empty, so use it only when you plan to put new laws in place afterwards.

label: All travel plan modifier copies
summary: Removes every copy of the named modifier from the travel plan.

label: Artifact feature group
summary: Removes the feature chosen from the given group from the artifact.
details: Groups the artifact requires cannot be removed. The value is the group's key. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Artifact modifier
summary: Removes a static modifier from the artifact.
details: The value is the modifier's name; a duration is not supported. Vanilla most often removes `artifact_placeholder_modifier`.

label: Barter goods
summary: Removes barter goods from the character.
details: The game's documentation says nothing more. Vanilla uses it once, with a saved scope called `scope:barter`, so the value is probably a saved barter; this is an inference from that single use.

label: Bonus fascination
summary: Removes the culture's current bonus fascination (the innovation chosen as its bonus).
details: You do not need to remove it before picking a different innovation, because the new choice replaces the old one. Written as `remove_bonus_fascination_innovation = yes` inside a culture.

label: Building
summary: Removes a building from the province.
details: The value is the building's name. Vanilla also uses template placeholders such as `$BUILDING$_01` inside scripted effects, and removes a great project's under-construction building.

label: Traveler
summary: Takes a character off the travel plan.
details: The owner of the travel plan cannot be removed. Vanilla passes saved scopes or `root` and `prev`.

label: Character flag
summary: Removes a flag from the character.
details: A flag is a named marker that script sets and later checks. Vanilla uses it very often, mostly with a plain flag name.

label: Character modifier
summary: Removes a modifier from the character.
details: The value is the modifier's name. If the modifier was added several times, see `remove_all_character_modifier_instances`; the game's documentation does not say how many copies this one removes.

label: Realm from sub-region
summary: Removes all of the given character's de facto counties from the situation sub-region.
details: De facto means the counties the character's realm actually holds. Runs on a situation sub-region; the value is the character. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Secret faith
summary: Removes the character's secret faith.
details: Written as `remove_character_secret_faith = yes`.

label: Claim
summary: Removes an explicit claim the character has on the given title.
details: Only claims that were given directly are removed, not claims the character gets from a living parent or grandparent.

label: Clerical realm from sub-region
summary: Removes all counties of the given clerical title's realm from the situation sub-region.
details: Runs on a situation sub-region; the value is the title.

label: Commander
summary: Removes the commander currently leading the army.
details: Written as `remove_commander = yes`.

label: Concubine
summary: Ends the given character's role as a concubine of the character.
details: The character the effect runs on is the one who keeps the concubine; the value is the concubine.

label: Confederation member
summary: Removes the given character from the confederation.
details: The holder of the confederation title cannot be removed. The documented usage line spells the key `remove_member`, while vanilla writes `remove_confederation_member`.

label: Confederation member house
summary: Removes the given house from the confederation.
details: The documented usage line spells the key `remove_member_house`, while the key listed, and the one vanilla uses, is `remove_confederation_member_house`.

label: County modifier
summary: Removes a modifier from the county.
details: The value is the modifier's name.

label: Courtier or guest
summary: Removes a courtier or guest from the host character's court.
details: Without a new place, the removed character is moved to the pool and stays in the same province. With the block form you can name a new location.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The courtier or guest to remove.

fields.name: new_location
fields.text: The province the character is moved to.

label: Culture tradition
summary: Removes the given tradition from the culture.
details: The value is the tradition's name, for example `tradition_court_eunuchs`.

label: Dead character variable
summary: Removes a variable from a dead character.
details: The value is the variable's name. Vanilla does not use it.
